nodes.label: Watch Party LAN prototype
nodes.rationale: Host-run LAN watch party using plain HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript with Node.js, Express, Socket.IO and HTTP video streaming. No frontend build step or database.

nodes.label: Persistent LAN host server
nodes.rationale: Guests use a reachable LAN address on the same network. The original server computer must remain running even after browser closure or host-role transfer; transferring the host role does not move the server or uploaded files.

nodes.label: Authenticated HTTP uploaded-video delivery
nodes.rationale: MP4, WebM and OGV uploads travel through multipart HTTP and stream from local disk with HTTP range support rather than through Socket.IO. Default upload limit is 2 GB; no transcoding occurs. Replaced sources and expired rooms trigger cleanup; graceful shutdown removes the process upload directory, while crashes can leave files behind.

nodes.label: YouTube IFrame API playback
nodes.rationale: Each guest streams directly from YouTube. Embedding requires internet access and an HTTP-served page; unavailable videos, embedding restrictions, loading failures and autoplay restrictions have visible handling.

nodes.label: Server-authoritative playback commands
nodes.rationale: Only the host may play, pause, seek or select sources, with server-side validation. Commands are ordered, per-video IDs reject controls for replaced sources, and snapshots restore late arrivals or reconnects. Volume, mute and fullscreen are local controls.

nodes.label: Server-timestamp playback anchor
nodes.rationale: Play, pause and seek update a server-time anchor so late arrivals receive the calculated current position. Clients do not continuously correct playback; buffering, ads, suspended tabs and network delay can cause drift.

nodes.label: Room-scoped chat protocol
nodes.rationale: Separate Socket.IO chat events avoid changing playback or rebroadcasting full video state. Membership is required and sender identity comes from the server session. Plain-text messages allow 1,000 Unicode code points and six accepted messages per participant per five seconds. Each room retains 100 messages and 400 accepted IDs for retry deduplication; page-local drafts survive connection loss.

nodes.label: Room membership and host lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Rooms use six-character codes or invites and allow 20 members including disconnected sessions. Host disconnection reserves the role for 20 seconds before online failover; explicit leave transfers immediately. Reconnect sessions last ten minutes, explicit leave removes a session, and empty rooms expire. In-memory rooms, messages and sessions are lost on restart.

nodes.label: Invite-prototype media access control
nodes.rationale: Uploads require the connected host's room token and media access requires a participant token. Public snapshots omit tokens and upload paths. Room codes are invitations rather than passwords; public deployment requires HTTPS, user authentication, storage quotas and deployment hardening.

nodes.label: Deferred features and performance work
nodes.rationale: Discovery, recommendations, filters/search, standalone reactions, playlists, polls, continuous drift correction, clock synchronization and latency optimization are deferred. The edition claims neither p99 latency nor drift targets.
